He was a local lord ([[:en:Kokujin|Kokujin]]) of {{ill|Shinano Province|ckb|پارێزگای شینانۆ|cs|Provincie Šinano|de|Provinz Shinano|eo|Provinco Ŝinano|es|Provincia de Shinano|fa|ولایت شینانو|fr|Province de Shinano|gl|Provincia de Shinano|hak|Shinano-koet|id|Provinsi Shinano|it|Shinano (provincia)|ja|信濃国|knc|Shinano Province|ko|시나노국|lt|Šinano žemė|ms|Wilayah Shinano|nl|Shinano (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Shinano|pt|Província de Shinano|ru|Синано (провинция)|simple|Shinano Province|sk|Šinano (provincia)|sr|Провинција Шинано|th|แคว้นชินาโนะ|tr|Shinano (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сінано|zh|信濃國|zh_min_nan|Sinano-kok|zh_yue|信濃國|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}, serving as the lord of {{ill|Takatō Castle|de|Burg Takatō|es|Castillo de Takatō|fa|قلعه تاکاتوئو|fr|Château de Takatō|ja|高遠城|ko|다카토성|ml|ടകറ്റോ കാസിൽ|zh|高遠城|qid=Q11672954|lt=Takato Castle}} (located in present-day {{ill|Ina, Nagano|ar|إنا (ناغانو)|azb|اینا، ناقانو|ce|Ина (гӀала)|ceb|Ina (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Ina (Nagano)|es|Ina (Nagano)|fa|اینا، ناگانو|fi|Ina (Nagano)|fr|Ina (Nagano)|gl|Ina|hy|Ինա (քաղաք)|id|Ina, Nagano|it|Ina (Nagano)|ja|伊那市|ko|이나시|mzn|اینا، ناگانو|nl|Ina (Nagano)|pl|Ina (miasto)|pt|Ina (Nagano)|ro|Ina|ru|Ина (город)|sv|Ina, Nagano|tg|Ина|th|อินะ|tl|Ina, Nagano|tr|Ina, Nagano|tt|Ина (шәһәр)|uk|Іна (Наґано)|ur|اینا، ناگانو|uz|Ina (Nagano)|vi|Ina, Nagano|war|Ina, Nagano|zh|伊那市|zh_classical|伊那市|zh_min_nan|Ina-chhī|zh_yue|伊那|qid=Q840888|lt=Ina, Nagano}}, {{ill|Takatō, Nagano|fa|تاکاتوئو، ناگانو|ja|高遠町|ko|다카토정|qid=Q7677451|lt=Takato Town}}). As a retainer of the {{ill|Takeda clan|ja|甲斐武田氏}}, he held the position of {{ill|Sakikata-shū|ja|信濃先方衆}} in charge of the Shinano frontlines. He belonged to the {{ill|Q11672957|fa|خاندان تاکاتوئو|ja|高遠氏|qid=Q11672957}}, a cadet branch of the {{ill|Suwa clan|de|Suwa (Klan)|fa|خاندان سووا|fr|Clan Suwa|id|Klan Suwa|it|Clan Suwa|ja|諏訪氏|ko|스와씨|pt|Clã Suwa|ru|Сува (род)|qid=Q2975376|lt=Suwa clan}}, and sometimes used the Suwa surname. His official titles included Shinano-no-Kami and Kii-no-Kami. Yoritsugu was the son and heir of Takato Mitsunari (Shinano-no-Kami) and married the daughter of {{ill|Suwa Yorimitsu|fa|سووا یوریمیتسو|fr|Suwa Yorimitsu|ja|諏訪頼満 (安芸守)|qid=Q7650544|lt=Suwa Yorimitsu (Aki-no-Kami)}}.

== Biography ==
Yoritsugu is said to have been the son or grandson of {{ill|Takato Tsugimune|ja|高遠継宗}}, who opposed the Suwa main family during internal conflicts. After {{ill|Q11631959|ja|諏訪頼満|qid=Q11631959}} unified the Suwa clan, Yoritsugu initially resisted but eventually became a vassal and married Yorimitsu’s daughter.

During the Sengoku period, the Takeda clan of {{ill|Kai Province|ckb|پارێزگای کای|cs|Provincie Kai|de|Provinz Kai|eo|Provinco Kai|es|Provincia de Kai|eu|Kai probintzia|fa|ولایت کای|fi|Kain provinssi|fr|Province de Kai|gl|Provincia de Kai|id|Provinsi Kai|it|Kai (provincia)|ja|甲斐国|ko|가이국|lt|Kajaus žemė|ms|Wilayah Kai|nl|Kai (provincie)|pt|Província de Kai|ru|Каи (провинция)|simple|Kai Province|sk|Kai (provincia)|sr|Провинција Каи|tr|Kai (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кай|wuu|甲斐国|zh|甲斐國|zh_min_nan|Kai-kok|zh_yue|甲斐國|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province}} and the Suwa clan of Shinano Province had a long-standing alliance. However, in Tenbun 10 (1542), {{ill|Takeda Shingen|ar|تاكيدا شين-غن|az|Takeda Şingen|ban|Takeda Shingen|ca|Takeda Shingen|cs|Šingen Takeda|de|Takeda Shingen|eo|Takeda Shingen|es|Takeda Shingen|fa|تاکدا شینگن|fi|Takeda Shingen|fr|Takeda Shingen|hak|Takeda Shingen|he|טקדה שינגן|hu|Takeda Singen|id|Takeda Shingen|it|Takeda Shingen|ja|武田信玄|jv|Takeda Shingen|ko|다케다 신겐|nl|Takeda Shingen|no|Takeda Shingen|pl|Shingen Takeda|pt|Takeda Shingen|ru|Такэда Сингэн|sk|Šingen Takeda|sq|Takeda Shingen|sr|Такеда Шинген|sv|Takeda Shingen|th|ทาเกดะ ชิงเง็ง|tr|Takeda Shingen|uk|Такеда Шінґен|vi|Takeda Shingen|wuu|武田信玄|zh|武田信玄|zh_min_nan|Takeda Singen|zh_yue|武田信玄|zu|Takeda Shingen|qid=Q276404}} (later known as Takeda Shingen) ascended as the Takeda clan head and began an aggressive campaign to conquer Shinano, breaking the alliance and invading the Suwa domain. Yorishige was taken to {{ill|Q11577765|ja|甲府|qid=Q11577765}} and forced to commit suicide later that month. The Suwa domain was divided between the Takeda and Yoritsugu, with Yoritsugu controlling the western half.

Yoritsugu, aiming to restore the Suwa clan's authority, allied with {{ill|Q11624578|fa|فوجیساوا یوریچیکا|ja|藤沢頼親|zh|藤澤賴親|qid=Q11624578}} of {{ill|Q11591217|fa|قلعه فوکویو|ja|福与城|qid=Q11591217}} in {{ill|Ina district|ja|伊那郡|qid=Q11380911}} to invade Takeda territory. After the castle’s capture, the Takeda fortified Takato Castle as a strategic base for controlling Shinano.

In Tenbun 17 (1548), after the Takeda’s defeat at the {{ill|Battle of Uedahara|ca|Batalla d'Uedahara|es|Batalla de Uedahara|eu|Uedaharako gudua|fa|نبرد اوئه‌داهارا|fr|Bataille de Uedahara|he|הקרב על אוהדהרה|it|Battaglia di Uedahara|ja|上田原の戦い|ko|우에다하라 전투|nl|Slag bij Uedahara|zh|上田原之戰|qid=Q1358091|lt=Battle of Uedahara}} against {{ill|Murakami Yoshikiyo|fa|موراکامی یوشیکیو|fr|Murakami Yoshikiyo|it|Murakami Yoshikiyo|ja|村上義清|ko|무라카미 요시키요|nl|Murakami Yoshikiyo|uk|Муракамі Йосікійо|zh|村上義清|qid=Q1048622|lt=Murakami Yoshikiyo}}, unrest spread in Takeda-controlled territories. Yoritsugu continued serving the Takeda but was reportedly forced to commit suicide during a campaign in {{ill|Minami Shinshū area|ja|南信州地域|qid=Q11666112}} in Tenbun 21 (1552). His posthumous name was 大用普徹大禅定院 (Daiyō Futtetsu Daizendō-in). Following his death, {{ill|Hoshina Masatoshi|fa|هوشینا ماساتوشی|fr|Hoshina Masatoshi|it|Hoshina Masatoshi|ja|保科正俊|nl|Hoshina Masatoshi|zh|保科正俊|qid=Q2040645|lt=Hoshina Masatoshi}}, a vassal of the Takato clan, rose to prominence under the Takeda. While traditionally believed to mark the Takato clan's extinction, recent studies suggest that {{ill|Takeda Katsuyori|ar|تاكيدا كاتسويوري|cs|Kacujori Takeda|de|Takeda Katsuyori|eo|Takeda Katsuyori|es|Takeda Katsuyori|eu|Takeda Katsuyori|fa|تاکدا کاتسویوری|fr|Takeda Katsuyori|id|Takeda Katsuyori|it|Takeda Katsuyori|ja|武田勝頼|ko|다케다 가쓰요리|ms|Takeda Katsuyori|nl|Takeda Katsuyori|pl|Katsuyori Takeda|pt|Takeda Katsuyori|ro|Takeda Katsuyori|ru|Такэда Кацуёри|sr|Такеда Кацујори|th|ทาเกดะ คัตสึโยริ|tr|Takeda Katsuyori|uk|Такеда Кацуйорі|zh|武田勝賴|zh_min_nan|Takeda Katuyori|qid=Q662482|lt=Takeda Katsuyori}}, Takeda Shingen's fourth son, inherited the Takato-Suwa lineage.<ref>Marushima Kazuhiro, "Kōyasan Jōkei-in's *Kōkoku Kako-chō*: The *Past Records of Kōshū Monthly Memorials*," *Takeda Clan Studies,* No. 34, 2006.</ref>
